name: Erlebnistherme Zillertal
kurzbeschreibung: The Erlebnistherme Zillertal in Fügen offers vibrant aquatic fun, thrilling water slides, and a generous wellness and sauna world for the entire family.
preis: Admission charges apply (flexible tickets for leisure pool, sauna zone, and families)
beschreibung:
Overview

Erlebnistherme Zillertal in Fügen is the premier aquatic, spa, and wellness destination in the Zillertal. Operating year-round in all weather conditions, this state-of-the-art thermal bath complex covers thousands of square metres, seamlessly uniting high-energy family fun with restorative alpine wellness. Swimmers and adventure enthusiasts delight in dynamic leisure pools featuring counter-current channels, bubbling geysers, and surging wave pools. The headline attractions are the two giant water slides, including western Austria's longest slide at 133 metres equipped with dynamic multimedia light and audio effects. For those seeking tranquility, the expansive adult sauna and spa village provides scented herbal saunas, steam grottoes, outdoor brine pools, and relaxation lounges overlooking the Zillertal Alps.

Route & Requirements

Visiting the thermal baths is simple, safe, and relaxing for guests of all generations. The entire complex is barrier-free and fully wheelchair-accessible, equipped with wide corridors, ramped pool entries, and water access hoists. Families with toddlers enjoy a dedicated, warm shallow water adventure zone with miniature slides and gentle water toys. Guests should bring swimwear, towels, and non-slip pool slippers; rental bathrobes and towels are available at reception for a modest fee. A stay of three to four hours or a full-day ticket is recommended to fully enjoy both the thermal adventure pools and sauna village.

Visiting & Getting There

The thermal baths are situated on the southern outskirts of Fügen in the lower Zillertal. From Jenbach rail junction, the scenic Zillertal Railway (Zillertalbahn) drops passengers at Fügen-Hart station, just a ten-minute stroll from the baths. Local ski and hiking buses stop directly outside the entrance pavilion. Motorists will find ample free parking and EV charging points in front of the building. The complex is open daily year-round. Purchasing tickets online beforehand guarantees fast, contactless entry during peak periods.

Tips

Following a day on the ski slopes or hiking trails, soak in the heated outdoor saltwater pool at 34°C, where underwater jets soothe tired muscles beneath the open sky. Sauna enthusiasts should not miss the hourly ceremonial steam infusions (Aufguss) featuring natural alpine pine and herbal essences. The thermal spa restaurant serves fresh salads, regional Tyrolean dishes, and refreshing smoothies inside both the family pool and quiet sauna zones.
